one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 4 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: Checks 1–2 test only what their words require: padding with fill, the space default, and returning s unchanged when long enough. Check 3 breaks: the expect line asks for "a section for every function", but the regex '^#{1,6} +' + f + '\\b' also requires an ATX heading that starts with the function name. A section titled "The padLeft function", or one with an underlined (setext) heading, would fail. Its FAIL condition "a heading with no describing text" adds a further judgement. Check 4 breaks: "npm test passes" needs only a passing run (exit=0), yet PASS also requires "the output shows `# fail 0`", exact reporter wording the words don't force. None of these stricter conditions is under the Advisory heading.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. `npm test` maps to the existing script `node --test`, and test/strutil.test.js exists. The `node --input-type=module -e "..."` scripts import `./index.js`, which is tracked, and `node:assert/strict` and `node:fs`, which are built-in modules. They use valid ESM syntax. The escaping is correct: inside bash double quotes, `'\\\\b'` becomes `'\\b'`, which the JS string turns into the regex `\b`. That gives `^#{1,6} +name\b` with the `m` flag. No `$` or backticks get expanded by mistake. The `!` in `!new RegExp` only triggers history expansion in interactive shells, not in a normal non-interactive agent shell. `; echo exit=$?` is valid. The files the briefs edit exist, and git and PR steps are standard. One small doubt: Check 4's pass line expects `# fail 0`, which is TAP output and may differ by reporter. That affects how the result is read, not whether the command runs.

catches-traps.why: The briefs handle all three must_catch items. (1) Builder step 2 says README.md has "NOT [a section] for slugify, which index.js already exports" and tells the builder to add a "## slugify(s)" section as well as a "## padLeft(s, width, fill)" section. (2) Verifier Check 3 reads index.js at the PR head and prints its exported functions. It fails if any of them lack a README heading. Its PASS line names "at least capitalize, slugify, truncate, padLeft", and its FAIL line says "slugify had no section before this change, so it must be added too". (3) Verifier Check 1 asserts `m.padLeft('ab', 4)` equals '  ab', so it calls padLeft without a fill argument and checks that it pads with spaces. I found no part of either brief that contradicts these items.

avoids-must-not.why: Must_not 1 holds: Check 3 lists every exported function and fails if any, including slugify, has no README section ("slugify had no section before this change, so it must be added too"). Must_not 2 breaks in two places. First, Check 3 only counts a section when a heading matches the regex `'^#{1,6} +' + f + '\\b'`, with the function name right after the hashes. A valid section titled "## `padLeft(s, width, fill)`" or "### Function: padLeft" would fail, so the check requires a README layout the line never asks for. Second, Check 4's PASS needs "the output shows `# fail 0`". That ties "npm test passes" to one test runner's output format, which is stricter than a zero exit with no failing tests. Checks 1 and 2 do not test parameter count or require fill to be one character.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief, and the builder brief contains the checker's own probes. Builder step 5 is a "Self-check" that is the exact same inline node script as verifier Check 3 (`const missing = fns.filter(f => !new RegExp('^#{1,6} +' + f ...`). It even uses the same pass condition: "must print `missing README sections: none` and exit 0". The repo's tests don't contain this script, and neither the expect lines nor the issue name it, so none of the allowed exceptions cover it. Builder steps 1 and 3 also copy input/expected-output pairs from verifier Checks 1 and 2 ('42',5,'0'→'00042'; 'ab',4→'  ab'; '12345'→'12345'; '123456'→'123456'). So the builder brief hands the builder the checker's methods, not just the bar.
